summary: Shutdown-time cleanup that destroys up to two windows and unregisters their window classes, then releases the cursor clip. If the primary window handle dword_7CE2E0 equals the secondary handle hWnd, the secondary is cleared first to avoid a double-destroy. The dword_7CE2E0 window uses the 'CubeRealTime' class; a distinct hWnd window uses ClassName. Returns the result of ClipCursor(0).

operations.description: When dword_7CE2E0 equals hWnd, clear the local v0 and reset global hWnd to 0 to avoid destroying the same window twice.
When dword_7CE2E0 is non-NULL, destroy it, unregister its 'CubeRealTime' window class, and zero the global.
UnregisterClassA(aCuberealtime, hinst) for the primary window class.
Set dword_7CE2E0 to 0 after destroying the primary window.
When the captured secondary handle v0 is non-NULL, destroy that window too.
UnregisterClassA(ClassName, hinst) for the secondary window class.
Reset global hWnd to 0 after destroying the secondary window.
Return ClipCursor(0) to release the cursor clip rectangle.

unresolved: Why dword_7CE2E0's window is re-fetched (v0 = hWnd) inside the first destroy branch is not evidenced.
The two window classes' ownership (which subsystem creates each window) is caller-supplied and unknown here.
hinst and the global function pointers are imported values; their initialization site is outside this function.
